# Defining Goals and Choosing Components

Welcome to the **Capstone Project**. Across the previous twelve chapters, we analyzed the theory, architecture, and engineering trade-offs of modern Linux subsystems. In this chapter, we synthesize these lessons into an end-to-end, bootable operating system built from source: **BYOL (Build Your Own Linux)**.

```
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
|                 BYOL Capstone Architecture                  |
|                                                             |
| Operating System Name:     BYOL Linux                       |
| CPU Architecture:          x86_64                           |
| C Standard Library:        musl-libc (Ultra-lean & secure)  |
| Core Utilities:            BusyBox + Selected GNU tools     |
| Linux Kernel:              Upstream 6.10 Longterm Branch    |
| Init & Service Management: OpenRC / BusyBox Init            |
| Storage & Early Boot:      Custom Initramfs + OverlayFS     |
| Package Manager:           byol-pkg (JSON repo + zstd tar)  |
| Installation Media:        Hybrid BIOS/UEFI Live ISO        |
| Testing Harness:           QEMU / KVM Virtualization        |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
```

## Architectural Design Principles

For our capstone distribution, we balance transparency, compilation speed, and production rigor:

1. **Lightweight & Fast Compilation:** By choosing `musl-libc` and a hybrid BusyBox/GNU userland, the entire operating system compiles in under 45 minutes on a modern 8-core computer, avoiding the 10+ hour build times of full enterprise distributions.
2. **Strict Independence:** The target distribution contains zero dynamic linkages to the host operating system. It boots autonomously on physical silicon or virtual machines.
3. **Reproducible ISO Output:** The entire build pipeline is codified into deterministic shell scripts and recipes that can run unattended inside continuous integration environments.

Let us begin by establishing the isolated build environment.
